metadata.Name: PIQA
metadata.Description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning, called Physical Interaction: Question Answering (PIQA). It presents questions as a goal and two possible solutions, requiring a model to choose the most sensible one. The dataset focuses on everyday situations and atypical solutions, inspired by how-to instructions from instructables.com.
Provider: Paul G. Allen School for Computer Science and Engineering, University of Washington
metadata.Paper Title: PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language
metadata.Venue Title: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fourth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
Affiliations: Paul G. Allen School for Computer Science and Engineering, University of Washington
metadata.Abstract: To apply eyeshadow without a brush, should I use a cotton swab or a toothpick? Questions requiring this kind of physical commonsense pose a challenge to today's natural language understanding systems. While recent pretrained models (such as BERT) have made progress on question answering over more abstract domains -- such as news articles and encyclopedia entries, where text is plentiful -- in more physical domains, text is inherently limited due to reporting bias. Can AI systems learn to reliably answer physical commonsense questions without experiencing the physical world?nnIn this paper, we introduce the task of physical commonsense reasoning and a corresponding benchmark dataset Physical Interaction: Question Answering or PIQA. Though humans find the dataset easy (95% accuracy), large pretrained models struggle (~77%). We provide analysis about the dimensions of knowledge that existing models lack, which offers significant opportunities for future research.
